Here is a four-sentence explanation of recursion for a beginner:

Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller or simpler version of that same problem. To work correctly, every recursive function must have a base case—a condition that stops the self-calls—otherwise it will loop forever. Each call peels off a piece of the problem, and when the base case is finally reached, the function returns values back up the chain, combining them to produce the final answer. Think of it like a set of Russian nesting dolls: you keep opening a smaller doll until you reach the tiniest one, and then you can put them all back together.
